questions.q: Distinguish between distance and displacement, and between speed and velocity.

answer.text: Distance is the total length of the path travelled by an object; it is a scalar quantity, having only magnitude. Displacement is the shortest distance from the starting point to the final position, measured in a straight line with direction; it is a vector quantity. Displacement can even be zero — for example, when an object returns to its starting point — while the distance covered is not.

Speed is the distance travelled per unit time and is a scalar. Velocity is the displacement per unit time and is a vector, being the speed of an object in a particular direction. Thus speed tells us how fast an object moves, while velocity tells us how fast and in which direction.

questions.q: State the equations of motion and explain what velocity–time graphs show.

answer.text: For an object moving with uniform acceleration, three equations relate the initial velocity u, final velocity v, acceleration a, time t and displacement s. They are v equals u plus a t; s equals u t plus half a t squared; and v squared equals u squared plus two a s. Using these, any unknown quantity can be found if the others are known.

In a velocity–time graph, the slope of the line gives the acceleration of the object, and the area under the line gives the distance travelled. A horizontal line means constant velocity, or zero acceleration, while a sloping straight line means uniform acceleration.

answer.text: give a clear picture of how an object moves over time.
